newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia King says decides not to abdicate.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia King says decides not to abdicate.

text.p: Cambodian King Norodom Sihanouk on Monday said he had decided not to abdicate, but also vowed not to return to the political arena in his troubled nation.
"After having weighed the pros and cons for many nights, I decide to remain as king for some time longer," Sihanouk said in a statement faxed to reporters.
Opponents of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who seized power in Cambodia last month, had called for Sihanouk to abdicate, but the king said he did not want to abandon his people.
"This is something that a king worthy of the name does not do," he said.

The king, who met Hun Sen and newly appointed First Prime Minister Ung Huot in Beijing last week, said he had already made clear his condemnation of the second prime minister's ousting of his son Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Poor health and Cambodia's political situation had so far prevented him from returning to his Southeast Asian homeland, Sihanouk said. He added that he still planned to return before the end of August but that he would stay far away from politics.
